title: Cut your video automatically on Mac · AgenticCutter
excerpt: Filler words, pauses and retakes removed automatically, locally on your Mac, no upload. You approve, the agent renders. 7-day free trial.
content_html:
Your agentic cutter.

Cut your video automatically, locally on your Mac. The agent builds the rough cut while you keep filming.

AgenticCutter is a local, agentic video cutter for macOS. You say what should stay, the cutter does the rest: filler words out, pauses tightened, the clean take remains. Driven through Claude Code or Codex, no clicking through waveforms.

Download for macOS

AgenticCutter 0.1.7 · DMG, 314 MB · notarized by Apple · Apple Silicon, macOS 26 or newer

Free for 7 days, then a subscription or a one-time purchase. Requires macOS 26 (Tahoe) or newer on an Apple Silicon Mac plus a Claude/Codex account or LM Studio.

See it in action: Propose, Approve, Render

Less explaining, more showing. In about 25 seconds you see the whole path: you say what you want, the agent cuts.

Animated product walkthrough, not a screen recording. Shows a typical editing task from start to finish.

Edit your video by talking to it.

The app, screen by screen

Seven images prepared for the Mac App Store. The window frames are rebuilt; every label inside them is a string from the app.

Eight phases, one track

Scene 02 · The Problem

Editing eats your hours, not shooting.

Shooting is the fast part. Then you sit in the editor for hours repeating the same three moves: cut the uh, trim the pause, delete the stumble. Mechanical work that keeps you from the next video.

  • Removing filler words and pauses costs hours per video.
  • You hunt for words in waveforms instead of reading them in a transcript.
  • Every retake needs to be found manually, reviewed, and deleted.

You edit words, the cutter cuts the video.

AgenticCutter transcribes your recording and shows you the edit as text. You say in plain language what should happen: tighten it, keep the take, cut harder. The cutter suggests, you approve, it renders. Controlled directly from Claude Code or Codex, everything on your machine.

AgenticCutter

Scene 03 · How it works

How it works

Three steps from raw footage to finished video. You stay in control, the cutter does the work.

  1. Suggest

    The cutter transcribes your recording and shows you the cut as text. Filler words, pauses, and slip-ups are highlighted so you see at a glance what can go.

  2. Approve

    You read the transcript and say in plain language what should stay: cut tighter, keep a take, remove the ums. You decide, the cutter executes.

  3. Render

    The cutter edits and exports locally as mp4 or ProRes. Your video is not uploaded or rendered in the cloud during that step.

Scene 04 · What for

What AgenticCutter actually handles

Six editing jobs you still do by hand today. AgenticCutter takes care of them automatically, right inside your timeline.

  • Shorten pauses

    Long silences between sentences are compressed to a natural length so your video flows without sounding rushed.

  • Cut out stumbles (in progress)

    AgenticCutter spots broken words and retakes in the transcript. Detection is built, wiring into app and CLI follows, today you mark them yourself.

  • Trim starts and ends

    Dead air and long pauses at the start and end of a clip are trimmed so every sequence gets straight to the point.

  • Select the best take (in progress)

    With several takes of the same passage the strongest one should be suggested. Detection is built, wiring follows, today you pick it yourself.

For those who cut their own videos.

If you know your footage, like your voice, and still have no interest in spending another hour in the editor, the cutter is built for you.

  • Solo YouTubers who already work with Claude Code or Codex and publish regularly.

  • Course creators who need clean cuts lesson by lesson.

  • Privacy-conscious Mac users who want nothing uploaded to the cloud.

  • Dev YouTubers recording live coding: the screencast profile keeps the pauses where something is happening on screen.

  • Small agencies cutting for clients: client footage never leaves the Mac, batch runs go through the CLI.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where do my videos go? Are they stored on external servers?

Nowhere. Your video stays on your Mac. Transcription runs with mlx-whisper, cutting with ffmpeg, rendering locally. No upload, no external server sees your footage, only the transcript text for the cut decision goes to the cut-brain (more on that in the next question).

Can I use my own LLM? And what about Claude Code or Codex?

Yes. Your video footage always stays local on the Mac. If you steer via Claude Code or Codex, your edit instructions go to that provider. To keep the entire loop offline, connect a local LLM via LM Studio, and no copy leaves your machine.

When can I download AgenticCutter?

The download is live: get AgenticCutter for macOS via the download button on this page. The first 7 days are free, then you choose a subscription or a one-time purchase.

Does AgenticCutter run on Windows or Linux?

Currently macOS only, from version 26 with Apple silicon. The app is built natively in Swift and uses Apple silicon directly for local transcription, which is why there is no Windows or Linux build.

How do I control the cutter? Do I need to code?

You work through the native macOS app with drag and drop, a Review UI, and an Approve Gate. Or you control the cutter directly via Claude Code or Codex using natural language. The cutter proposes, you approve, it renders.

What does AgenticCutter cost?

Try it free for 7 days, all you need is an email address. After that: €9.99 per month, €79 per year, or €149 once. The one-time purchase is limited to the first 100 and includes all future updates.

Is there any outbound data traffic? Is it GDPR-compliant?

Your footage always stays on your Mac. In the default setup, only the transcript text for the cut decision goes to the cut-brain (Claude Code or Codex), which is standard data processing like any cloud tool. If you want zero data leaving at all, enable a local LLM via LM Studio (Zero-Cloud mode), then no copy ever leaves your machine.

What does the cutter do today, and what is still in progress?

Fifteen features are already running, from filler-word removal to transcript-driven cuts to the native macOS app. Four more are visibly marked as in progress. We show the order openly rather than making vague promises.

Does the cut-brain cost extra?

If you already have a Claude or Codex subscription, the cut decision runs through it, with no extra cost per cut. Without a subscription you run LM Studio locally, which costs nothing but needs a model download.

How long does a cut take?

Two stages run on your Mac: first the transcription, then the render. On a long video each takes several minutes and depends on your Mac, the length and the resolution. You start the job and do something else, the app tells you when the proposal is ready.

Which video formats can I feed in? What comes out?

Anything ffmpeg can read: MOV and MP4 from OBS, ScreenFlow, Final Cut or your iPhone, ProRes from the camera. Out comes MP4 (H.264) or ProRes, optionally plus SRT subtitles and an EDL JSON with every cut decision.

Does AgenticCutter run on macOS 15 or older?

No. AgenticCutter requires macOS 26 or newer on an Apple Silicon Mac. The app uses new system APIs and the Neural Engine directly, and a backport to older versions is not planned. Intel Macs are not supported.

How much disk space and RAM do I need?

The download is a DMG of roughly 314 MB. On top of that come the local transcription models fetched on first launch, plus intermediate files in the order of magnitude of your raw footage. 16 GB of RAM is enough for a normal cut, with 24 GB you can also run a local language model through LM Studio.

Which languages does the cut work in?

The cut is optimised for German: filler-word detection, retake patterns and the brand glossary are built for German speakers. English works well too because the transcription is multilingual. Subtitles can additionally be translated into further languages.

May I cut client footage with it?

Yes. The licence does not restrict you to private use, contract work is covered. Because your footage never leaves the Mac, the video itself needs no data-processing agreement. If you use Claude or Codex as the cut brain, transcript text goes to that provider, check that against your client agreement. With LM Studio the text stays local too. Details are in the EULA.

On how many Macs may I use the licence?

With a paid licence you can activate the app on up to three Macs at the same time, one during the trial. You can release a device yourself in the app at any time and win the slot back, no support ticket needed. Passing the key on to third parties is not permitted.

What happens after the 7 days? Are my projects locked?

After 7 days you need a licence to start new cuts. Videos you already rendered, transcripts and project files are ordinary files in your output folder and stay fully yours, licence or not.

What happens if I cancel the subscription?

On cancellation the licence runs until the end of the paid period and then goes inactive. The one-time purchase never expires and includes all future updates. Whatever you already rendered is yours either way.

How local is "local" exactly? Which steps never go online?

Always local: transcription, cut execution, render, subtitle generation and visual search. Optionally in the cloud is only the cut DECISION when you use Claude Code or Codex as the cut brain, and that sends individual still frames and transcript text, never the video or the audio track itself. Subtitle translation and the YouTube upload are optional too and you start them yourself. With LM Studio as the cut brain nothing leaves your Mac at all.

How is AgenticCutter different from Descript, Recut, Timebolt or Gling?

Two things. First: your video is never uploaded, while Descript and Gling are cloud services. Second: you steer by instruction rather than by click, you say "keep the second take, cut tighter" instead of marking regions. Recut and Timebolt also cut locally, but along silence rather than along your words. The detailed comparison is on the comparison page.

Can I keep working on the cut in Final Cut, Premiere or DaVinci?

Yes. Next to the finished video AgenticCutter writes an EDL JSON with every cut decision. You can drop the rendered cut straight into your timeline or take the rough cut as a starting point and polish it by hand.

I do not know Claude Code or Codex. Can I still use this?

Yes. The macOS app does everything by drag and drop: pull the video in, look at the proposal, approve, export. You only need Claude Code or Codex if you also want to steer the cutter by chat. An account with one of the two is required though, or a local model through LM Studio.

Does it also cut screencasts where I demo something in silence?

Yes, that is what the screencast profile is for. Pauses where something is happening on screen, a build running, a menu opening, stay in. Only real dead air is shortened. For live coding that is the difference between usable and shredded.

Your agentic cutter.

Cut your video automatically, locally on your Mac. The agent builds the rough cut while you keep filming.

AgenticCutter is a local, agentic video cutter for macOS. You say what should stay, the cutter does the rest: filler words out, pauses tightened, the clean take remains. Driven through Claude Code or Codex, no clicking through waveforms.

Eight phases, one track

Scene 02 · The Problem

Editing eats your hours, not shooting.

Shooting is the fast part. Then you sit in the editor for hours repeating the same three moves: cut the uh, trim the pause, delete the stumble. Mechanical work that keeps you from the next video.

  • Removing filler words and pauses costs hours per video.
  • You hunt for words in waveforms instead of reading them in a transcript.
  • Every retake needs to be found manually, reviewed, and deleted.

You edit words, the cutter cuts the video.

AgenticCutter transcribes your recording and shows you the edit as text. You say in plain language what should happen: tighten it, keep the take, cut harder. The cutter suggests, you approve, it renders. Controlled directly from Claude Code or Codex, everything on your machine.

AgenticCutter

Scene 03 · How it works

它是如何运作的

Three steps from raw footage to finished video. You stay in control, the cutter does the work.

  1. SuggestThe cutter transcribes your recording and shows you the cut as text. Filler words, pauses, and slip-ups are highlighted so you see at a glance what can go.
  2. ApproveYou read the transcript and say in plain language what should stay: cut tighter, keep a take, remove the ums. You decide, the cutter executes.
  3. RenderThe cutter edits and exports locally as mp4 or ProRes. Your video is not uploaded or rendered in the cloud during that step.

Scene 04 · What for

What AgenticCutter actually handles

Six editing jobs you still do by hand today. AgenticCutter takes care of them automatically, right inside your timeline.

  • Shorten pausesLong silences between sentences are compressed to a natural length so your video flows without sounding rushed.
  • Cut out stumbles (in progress)AgenticCutter spots broken words and retakes in the transcript. Detection is built, wiring into app and CLI follows, today you mark them yourself.
  • Trim starts and endsDead air and long pauses at the start and end of a clip are trimmed so every sequence gets straight to the point.
  • Select the best take (in progress)With several takes of the same passage the strongest one should be suggested. Detection is built, wiring follows, today you pick it yourself.

For those who cut their own videos.

If you know your footage, like your voice, and still have no interest in spending another hour in the editor, the cutter is built for you.

  • Solo YouTubers who already work with Claude Code or Codex and publish regularly.
  • Course creators who need clean cuts lesson by lesson.
  • Privacy-conscious Mac users who want nothing uploaded to the cloud.
  • Dev YouTubers recording live coding: the screencast profile keeps the pauses where something is happening on screen.
  • Small agencies cutting for clients: client footage never leaves the Mac, batch runs go through the CLI.

常见问题解答

Where do my videos go? Are they stored on external servers?

Nowhere. Your video stays on your Mac. Transcription runs with mlx-whisper, cutting with ffmpeg, rendering locally. No upload, no external server sees your footage, only the transcript text for the cut decision goes to the cut-brain (more on that in the next question).

Can I use my own LLM? And what about Claude Code or Codex?

是的。 Your video footage always stays local on the Mac. If you steer via Claude Code or Codex, your edit instructions go to that provider. To keep the entire loop offline, connect a local LLM via LM Studio, and no copy leaves your machine.

When can I download AgenticCutter?

The download is live: get AgenticCutter for macOS via the download button on this page. The first 7 days are free, then you choose a subscription or a one-time purchase.

Does AgenticCutter run on Windows or Linux?

Currently macOS only, from version 26 with Apple silicon. The app is built natively in Swift and uses Apple silicon directly for local transcription, which is why there is no Windows or Linux build.

How do I control the cutter? Do I need to code?

You work through the native macOS app with drag and drop, a Review UI, and an Approve Gate. Or you control the cutter directly via Claude Code or Codex using natural language. The cutter proposes, you approve, it renders.

What does AgenticCutter cost?

Try it free for 7 days, all you need is an email address. After that: €9.99 per month, €79 per year, or €149 once. The one-time purchase is limited to the first 100 and includes all future updates.

Is there any outbound data traffic? Is it GDPR-compliant?

Your footage always stays on your Mac. In the default setup, only the transcript text for the cut decision goes to the cut-brain (Claude Code or Codex), which is standard data processing like any cloud tool. If you want zero data leaving at all, enable a local LLM via LM Studio (Zero-Cloud mode), then no copy ever leaves your machine.

What does the cutter do today, and what is still in progress?

Fifteen features are already running, from filler-word removal to transcript-driven cuts to the native macOS app. Four more are visibly marked as in progress. We show the order openly rather than making vague promises.

Does the cut-brain cost extra?

If you already have a Claude or Codex subscription, the cut decision runs through it, with no extra cost per cut. Without a subscription you run LM Studio locally, which costs nothing but needs a model download.

How long does a cut take?

Two stages run on your Mac: first the transcription, then the render. On a long video each takes several minutes and depends on your Mac, the length and the resolution. You start the job and do something else, the app tells you when the proposal is ready.

Which video formats can I feed in? What comes out?

Anything ffmpeg can read: MOV and MP4 from OBS, ScreenFlow, Final Cut or your iPhone, ProRes from the camera. Out comes MP4 (H.264) or ProRes, optionally plus SRT subtitles and an EDL JSON with every cut decision.

Does AgenticCutter run on macOS 15 or older?

No. AgenticCutter requires macOS 26 or newer on an Apple Silicon Mac. The app uses new system APIs and the Neural Engine directly, and a backport to older versions is not planned. Intel Macs are not supported.

How much disk space and RAM do I need?

The download is a DMG of roughly 314 MB. On top of that come the local transcription models fetched on first launch, plus intermediate files in the order of magnitude of your raw footage. 16 GB of RAM is enough for a normal cut, with 24 GB you can also run a local language model through LM Studio.

Which languages does the cut work in?

The cut is optimised for German: filler-word detection, retake patterns and the brand glossary are built for German speakers. English works well too because the transcription is multilingual. Subtitles can additionally be translated into further languages.

May I cut client footage with it?

是的。 The licence does not restrict you to private use, contract work is covered. Because your footage never leaves the Mac, the video itself needs no data-processing agreement. If you use Claude or Codex as the cut brain, transcript text goes to that provider, check that against your client agreement. With LM Studio the text stays local too. Details are in the EULA.

On how many Macs may I use the licence?

With a paid licence you can activate the app on up to three Macs at the same time, one during the trial. You can release a device yourself in the app at any time and win the slot back, no support ticket needed. Passing the key on to third parties is not permitted.

What happens after the 7 days? Are my projects locked?

After 7 days you need a licence to start new cuts. Videos you already rendered, transcripts and project files are ordinary files in your output folder and stay fully yours, licence or not.

What happens if I cancel the subscription?

On cancellation the licence runs until the end of the paid period and then goes inactive. The one-time purchase never expires and includes all future updates. Whatever you already rendered is yours either way.

How local is "local" exactly? Which steps never go online?

Always local: transcription, cut execution, render, subtitle generation and visual search. Optionally in the cloud is only the cut DECISION when you use Claude Code or Codex as the cut brain, and that sends individual still frames and transcript text, never the video or the audio track itself. Subtitle translation and the YouTube upload are optional too and you start them yourself. With LM Studio as the cut brain nothing leaves your Mac at all.

How is AgenticCutter different from Descript, Recut, Timebolt or Gling?

有两件事。 First: your video is never uploaded, while Descript and Gling are cloud services. Second: you steer by instruction rather than by click, you say "keep the second take, cut tighter" instead of marking regions. Recut and Timebolt also cut locally, but along silence rather than along your words. The detailed comparison is on the comparison page.

Can I keep working on the cut in Final Cut, Premiere or DaVinci?

是的。 Next to the finished video AgenticCutter writes an EDL JSON with every cut decision. You can drop the rendered cut straight into your timeline or take the rough cut as a starting point and polish it by hand.

I do not know Claude Code or Codex. Can I still use this?

是的。 The macOS app does everything by drag and drop: pull the video in, look at the proposal, approve, export. You only need Claude Code or Codex if you also want to steer the cutter by chat. An account with one of the two is required though, or a local model through LM Studio.

Does it also cut screencasts where I demo something in silence?

Yes, that is what the screencast profile is for. Pauses where something is happening on screen, a build running, a menu opening, stay in. Only real dead air is shortened. For live coding that is the difference between usable and shredded.
